summary: Iteration 4 (dual gateway + genealogy) backend & frontend testing complete. Backend: 21/21 pytest cases pass covering ISU register + OTP→ACTIVE, Invite register + pending_review (no OTP), invite_logs, admin pending recommender_stats, admin user-detail with recommender + invitees + stats, invite-log endpoint, status gating, Resend key non-exposure. Frontend: dual-gateway tabs swap fields correctly, ISU register → /verify, admin /admin shows 3 tabs (Initiation, Keys, Invite Log) with gate badges, recommender nickname, recommender stats. Detail modal opens with full genealogy (recommender + invitees + stats grid + Approve/Reject/Close). Mint key works.

minor.issue: Sets auth cookies before OTP verification; necessary for /verify-otp to authenticate but means an unverified user is implicitly signed in. require_active still blocks all sensitive routes — acceptable.
Same cookie-on-register pattern; user is signed in but blocked by require_active until admin approves.
OTP and password reset tokens are still logged at INFO level in plaintext (logger.info 'OTP for ...'). Convenient for testing; gate behind APP_ENV before production.
CORS_ORIGINS default '*' with allow_credentials=True is invalid per CORS spec; pin to REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL origin.

recommended_by_nickname falls back to email split — fine, but if recommender doc is missing it sets None for email (safe); inline N+1 lookup to users + 2 counts per pending row — acceptable for low volume.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1090 lines (was 970). Strongly recommend splitting into routers (auth_isu, auth_invite, admin_genealogy, posts, comments, messages) before iteration 5 — past 700-line guideline.

_log_invite is called from BOTH register_invite (Gate B) AND verify_otp (Gate A on activation). Good. But if OTP verify is retried after success it would be blocked by status check (only pending_email allowed) — safe.
consume_recommendation_code uses find_one then conditional update_one — race-safe, but does not assert update_one.modified_count==1; defensive check would catch lost-race silently consumed key.
admin_user_detail iterates `async for p in db.posts.find(...)` to sum likes — for a heavy author this is N posts in memory; aggregate pipeline ($sum likes_size + boost_likes) would scale better.
Resend API key: confirmed not present in any tested API response or rendered HTML. .env contains RESEND_API_KEY server-side only — good identity protection.
send_otp / send_admin_decision still awaited inline; if Resend hangs, request hangs. Wrap in asyncio.create_task with logging.
/api/admin/users/{uid}/reject still allows rejecting a pending_email (pre-OTP) user; UX OK but consider explicit confirmation in admin UI.

No rate limit on /api/auth/register/isu or /register/invite — potential abuse (mass-pending entries from a single key abuser is bounded by used:true; mass ISU-domain registrations are not). Add IP throttle.
test_credentials.md is outdated (still references the removed /api/auth/register endpoint and old flow). Should be updated to mention /register/isu and /register/invite.

success_rate.frontend: 100% smoke (dual-gateway tabs, ISU register→/verify, 3 admin tabs, detail modal with genealogy, mint key)
